Asana

Coordinate the work that takes a business from setup to scale.

AOfficial product ↗Open in the hierarchy →
Level 4Inspect the detail

Asana helps business teams coordinate projects, responsibilities, due dates, and recurring work. We can create an organized workspace for a company launch, marketing calendar, client onboarding, hiring operations, and internal requests. Each process has a template, a responsible person, an agreed deadline, and a review step. For a larger company, we can connect task changes to approved reporting and automation so founders and managers can understand progress without manually collecting updates from every team.

Useful outputs

  • Business launch, campaign, onboarding, and recurring operations templates.
  • Project ownership rules, task fields, reporting views, and team operating guidance.
  • Authorized API integration, webhook receiver, reconciliation process, and handover notes.

Where we can apply it

  • Company setup: launch checklist → owners and milestones → weekly progress review → operational handover.
  • Marketing delivery: campaign brief → asset production → stakeholder review → scheduled publication → learnings.
  • Client journey: signed scope → onboarding project → delivery milestones → approval → renewal preparation.
  • Scaled team: recurring operations template → distributed owners → escalation → portfolio review where the plan supports it.
01

Use case 1

Build a reusable launch template covering positioning, brand, website, lead capture, sales handoff, and support readiness.

02

Use case 2

Create a campaign calendar with content owners, dependencies, review stages, and publication dates.

03

Use case 3

Set up repeatable client onboarding and delivery projects from a scoped agreement to final handover.

04

Use case 4

Create hiring and employee onboarding checklists with role-specific owners and access requests.

Inputs we need

  • Client-owned Asana organization or workspace and approved administrator access.
  • Project templates, task owners, milestones, due-date rules, and external collaborator requirements.
  • OAuth application credentials and minimal required scopes; access to every subscribed resource.

Delivery sequence

  • Map business processes, agree task ownership and due-date rules, then build a template for each recurring workflow.
  • Configure project visibility, external collaborator access, and minimal OAuth scopes; test with representative roles.
  • Subscribe to selected task or project changes, complete the webhook secret handshake, and verify incoming signatures.
  • Run a pilot, handle missing or delayed events with reconciliation where required, and review project metrics with team leads.

Expert review points

  • Approve task templates, client visibility, confidential project access, and milestone definitions.
  • Test authentication expiry, signature verification, webhook failure handling, and periodic state reconciliation.

We confirm available integrations, plans, permissions, and data mapping before implementing these connection candidates.

  • Slack
  • n8n
  • HTTP APIs
  • Google Workspace
  • Reporting dashboards

Signals we can make visible

  • Milestone completion: completed milestones ÷ milestones due in the chosen period.
  • Overdue-task share: unfinished past-due tasks ÷ all unfinished tasks with due dates.
  • Approval turnaround: elapsed time from review request to approved or rejected decision.
  • Onboarding cycle time: elapsed time from confirmed start to completion of the agreed onboarding checklist.

We agree the source, population, period, denominator, and decision behind each measure.

Explore the metric library ↗
  • Rules, reporting, portfolios, and advanced governance depend on the selected plan and feature availability.
  • Tokens act within the authorized user and resource permissions; never use a broad personal token as an unreviewed company-wide integration.
  • Webhooks are not a replayable audit ledger and may miss events in exceptional circumstances; reconcile resource state when complete processing is required.
  • Due dates and completion records require consistent team usage to make the suggested metrics meaningful.
